div.p: The Canadian Writing Centres Association/L’Association canadienne des centres de rédaction (CWCA/ACCR) welcomes proposals for our 2027 collaborative conference titled “Rhetoric, Writing, Community, and Discourse.”

In taking “community” as our theme for this year’s annual conference, we are signalling two things. First, we want to explore the storying of writing centres as communities. Writing centres have previously been described in metaphors including the cosy place with couches and coffee pots (McKinney, 2013), or the writing centre as noise –a a sign of relationship, of connection, and of creating new realities and futures (Boquet, 2002). Still, others have challenged these grand narratives by discussing how the complexities of writing centre life coupled with institutional pressures can strain the development of community (Severino, 2023).

Second, we want to celebrate the larger community we can build by bringing our three professional organizations together. Through this combined conference with The Canadian Society for the Study of Rhetoric/La société canadienne pour l’étude de la rhétorique (RhetCan) and The Canadian Association for the Study of Discourse and Writing/Association canadienne de rédactologie (CASDW/ACR), we hope to draw on the insights of parallel thinkers, learn from each other, and share resources to support the work in our respective fields.

Truly, whether we experience our work as cosy, noisy, or strained, community helps us frame much about the theory and practice of writing centre work, especially in times of austerity and change. In the words of our current CWCA/ACCR president, Dr. Marci Prescott-Brown: “We need more of each other right now, not less.” CWCA/ACCR encourages writing centre professionals, tutors, administrators, and adjacent professionals to explore the ways in which their work is defined by human connection, shapes relationships, contributes to collaborative meaning making, or constrains community.
We invite you to consider some of the following questions:

ul.li: What does community in writing centre work mean? What does it look like?
How can we build an authentic/genuine community in and between our writing centres?
What barriers do we face to building community in the writing centre? How do we tackle those barriers?
What are the ways we unintentionally interfere with our own goals for creating community?
Who is included in the community of our writing centres? Who is excluded?
What connections can we draw between discussions about generative AI and community?
Other topics related to writing centre work and studies are welcome.

div.p: While the conference will be held in person at University of Victoria, CWCA/ACCR is also planning to provide one day as a hybrid option for attendees to join and present virtually via Zoom Events. We invite presenters to consider what modality they would prefer from the options below. Please note: we have a limited amount of space for virtual-only presentations.
Submissions can take the following shapes:

ul.li:
Individual presentation (15-20 minutes)
Submit a title and abstract of 250-300 words

Pre-constituted panel (3-4 presentations; 90 minutes total)
Include a title and overview of the entire panel, with titles and brief abstracts for each individual paper included in the panel, to a total of 300-500 words

Workshop (90 minutes)
Provide an abstract of 250-300 words explaining the rationale for the workshop, as well as an outline of what the workshop will look like (i.e., what activities will participants do)

Roundtable (90 minutes)
Provide an abstract of 250-300 words explaining the rationale for the roundtable or dialogue, explaining the target audience and what the discussion will centre on

div.p: Please submit a 250–300 word abstract (or a 300 - 500 word abstract for pre-constituted panels) that clearly outlines your topic, format, and relevance to the conference theme, as well as your connection to the broader field of writing centre studies. Submissions are welcome in either English or French.
Submit proposals through the Four Waves platform. For any inquiries, please contact cwcaconference@gmail.com
